statements.venue: Press release introducing the TEST AI Act
statements.quote: While AI holds enormous positive potential, this new technology must be tested thoroughly to ensure that it is used responsibly,
statements.context: Durbin and Sen. Luján introduced a bill directing federal agencies to build testbeds for evaluating AI systems.
statements.reason: Calls for testing and guardrails against misuse but names no catastrophic or serious risk from advanced AI itself.

statements.quote: We are currently living with the results of our failure to regulate Big Tech when it came to social media. Let’s not make the same mistake when it comes to AI,
statements.context: Durbin opposed a provision in the Republican budget bill that would have blocked state AI laws for ten years.
statements.reason: Argues for regulating AI and warns of deceptive, biased and potentially dangerous tools, without acknowledging catastrophic risk.

statements.venue: Press release introducing the AI LEAD Act with Sen. Hawley
statements.quote: Kids and adults across the country are turning to AI chatbots for advice and information, but greedy tech companies have designed these products to protect their own bottom line—not users’ safety
statements.context: Durbin and Hawley introduced a bill letting people sue AI companies under product liability law for harms caused by AI systems.
statements.reason: About chatbot harms to users and company liability, which is outside the scope of catastrophic risk.

slowdown.note: No statement found for or against slowing frontier AI development.

pause.note: No statement found on pausing frontier AI. His opposition to the 'AI pause provision' in June 2025 was about a freeze on state AI laws, not a pause on AI development.

intl.note: He did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter urging an AI agreement with China; his name is not among the 17 signatures on the letter itself. No other statement found.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Lead sponsor, with Sen. Luján, of the TEST AI Act of 2025, which would have federal agencies set up testbeds to evaluate AI systems.
Introduced the AI LEAD Act with Sen. Hawley, creating a federal product liability claim against AI companies for harms caused by their systems.
Previewed the AI LEAD Act at a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on harms from AI chatbots.
Did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter from 17 senators urging AI talks with China (checked against the signature pages of the letter).
Letter PDF hosted by Senate Commerce Committee Democrats, 23 September 2026
grade_reason: His AI statements since January 2025 are about testing, product liability, chatbot harms to children and state regulation; none found acknowledges catastrophic risk from AI.
